newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Alyn Corp backs Q4 forecasts.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Alyn Corp backs Q4 forecasts.

text.p: Alyn Corp expects to report a fourth-quarter loss of about $0.09 per share, in line with forecasts by analysts and the company, Robin Carden, its president and chief executive, said on Friday.
He said the company expected to generate revenues of less than $1 million in the quarter.

Carden said the expected results would reflect Alyn's focus and investment in building a plant in Irvine, California. The company, which makes advanced metal composites, will have the new facility up and running within a few weeks, he said.

Carden said the completion of the plant was a significant development for the company, enabling it to use its own proprietary blending methods rather than secondary sources. That will allow Alyn to boost production sharply.

"Our 1996 sales will be nothing compared to what we expect in 1997," Carden said. He estimated that revenues would reach between $12 million and $14 million and the company would break even in the year to December 31.
Toward that end, Carden said Alyn next week would announce the closing of a contract for "substantial" volumes of its metal alloy.
In September, Alyn signed a contract with Taylor Made Golf Co for the production of metalwood golf club heads, which it said achieve greater distance than those made of titanium.
The company also has contracts to make parts for bicycle frames, baseball bats and computer discs with superior storage capabilities, it said..

Carden said the company was also delivering on prototype requests by more than 30 companies interested in testing its metal alloys. Those companies are in industries ranging from sporting goods to transportation.
